To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) habitats dominated by small frondose brown algal species are more productive and structurally distinct from low-lying turf habitats and (b) these habitats support a distinct assemblages of associated macrofaunal communities.
habitats dominated by smaller fronds can be analogous to kelp forests, but are not analogous to turf-dominated habitats.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the structure and functioning (e.g. primary productivity, trophic structure, community composition) of two different shallow subtidal communities dominated by macroalgae, in the Azores (Portugal), and the comparison of these two communities with other well-known vegeted habitats (e.g kelp forests).
the role of habitat structure on ecosystem functioning, and how this role is influenced by the type of habitat structure (i.e. fronds versus turfs).

the role of two different types of shallow-water habitats (frondose and turf-dominated) on the functioning of subtidial reef ecosystems, and with the potential role of these ecosystems in supporting biodiversity and fisheries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure and functioning, in terms of productivity and community structure, is more related to algal biomass than to algal morphology.
the role of frondose algae is more important than that of turf algae in the structure and function of the subtidal community, but this is only valid for the specific conditions of the Azores.
the frondose habitat is a more productive, more structuring and a more species-rich habitat than the turf.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the absence of large kelp forests, smaller frondose macroalgae may provide a suitable habitat for many organisms, and may also be a key component in the functioning of subtidual reef ecosystems in warmer temperate waters.
, even in warmer temperate regions, vegetated macroalgal habitats are important for the structure and functioning in subtidal communities.

, although the role of vegetated habitats in structuring shallow subtidal communities has been well established for kelp and seagrass beds, it is still largely overlooked in the case of smaller brown macroalgal dominated communities, despite their wide distribution and ecological importance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
even in warmer temperate waters, where kelp forests and seagrass beds are largely absent, the role of other less notable vegetated habitats should not be underestimated.

, although the ecological role of vegetated habitats is often associated to the presence of large macroalgae (e.g. macrophytes), smaller frondose algae can also play a similar role in the structure of shallow subtidalecosystems.

even in the absence of large kelps forests and/or seagrass beds, other vegetated habitats (in this case, dominated by smaller fronds) can still play a key role on the structure and functioning shallow-water reef ecosystems.
